title: A Robot You Drive From a Chair: A Lossy, Delayed Link, a Stop Path on the Robot, and a Timeout Chosen From a Distance

questions.question: At 2 m/s and 1.5 m/s^2 of braking, what timeout stops the robot within a metre of the link going?
options: None: the braking alone is 1.333 m
questions.explanation: The answer is a lower speed. At 2 m/s the braking distance alone is 2 squared over twice 1.5, 1.333 m. No timeout can make that less than a metre.

questions.question: The link comes back after a stop, with no reset pressed. What does the robot do?
options: Goes on from where it stopped
Resets itself after a second of good link
Stays stopped: the link coming back is not permission, and a person presses reset after a second of good link
Goes on at half speed
questions.explanation: The stop is latched. With no reset it was still stopped at 40 s; with a person pressing reset after a second of good link it went on.

questions.question: A link that delays every packet by one second. How much farther does a robot at 1 m/s go after the link fails?
options: Nothing: a delayed packet is still a packet
Ten metres more
One metre more (1.598 m against 0.598 m): the delay is added at the speed
0.3 m more, the timeout
questions.explanation: Old commands keep arriving for a second after the link has really failed, and the robot keeps obeying them at 1 m/s.

questions.question: On a link that loses 20 percent, a timeout of 0.1 s did what over an hour?
options: 1198 false stops, with the robot stopped for 52.1 percent of the hour
3 false stops, stopped for 0.1 percent of the hour
No false stops
185 false stops, stopped for 5.5 percent
questions.explanation: Two heartbeats lost in a row has a chance of 0.04, and there are 72000 heartbeats in an hour. The robot spent more time stopped than moving.

questions.question: The robot's timeout is too short for the loss and too long for the distance. What is the answer?
options: A timeout half way between the two
No timeout at all
A longer wait before reset
Neither: a better link, or a lower speed
questions.explanation: The distance sets the longest timeout and the loss sets the shortest. When the first is below the second, no timeout satisfies both.

questions.question: Why does real radio make loss to the power k a poor guide?
options: Real loss comes in bursts
Real radio never loses packets
It is a good guide: losses are independent
The heartbeat rate changes with the loss
questions.explanation: False stops are rarer and real outages longer than the independent model says. The table assumes each packet is lost independently. A real link loses them in runs, so the same average loss gives fewer false stops and longer silences.
